new.pl: Lake Owen outlet on the Long Lake Branch of the White River, SW¼ SW¼ sec. 11 T44N R7W
new.st: Burnham (1929): Rust-Owen built logging dams about 1882, one "where it [the White River branch] leaves Lake Owen" and the other at Drummond. The Wisconsin DNR dam inventory lists the 'Lake Owen Outlet' dam on the Long Lake Branch of the White River, built 1880, in SW¼ SW¼ sec. 11 T44N R7W. See also the Drummond dam pin (bur-drummond-dam).
new.t: Chequamegon-Nicolet National Forest land: look only, no detecting or digging.
src: Burnham, The Lake Superior Country in History and in Story (1929), leaf 396
Wisconsin DNR dams database, key 765 'Lake Owen Outlet'
pinev: Placed from the Wisconsin DNR dam record (key 765), quarter-quarter SW SW sec. 11 T44N R7W (about 200 m).

new.n: Gilpatrick Lake (Lake Margaret) logging headquarters, Gull River Lumber Co. (about 1890)
new.pl: Lake Margaret (formerly Gilpatrick Lake), Lake Shore, just north of Gull Lake, Cass County
new.v: Chain, log dogs, spikes, camp trash
new.st: King (1981): the Gull River Lumber Co. narrow gauge ran 12 miles northwest from its mill plus 6 miles of spurs by 1890, with logging headquarters and a landing at 'Gilpatrick Lake (now known as Lake Margaret)'; logs were rafted across Gull Lake. Track ran on to Spider Lake, a 673-ft trestle crossed the Gull Lake narrows in 1892, and the Lake Hubert-Spider Lake track was pulled in 1894. The pin marks the lake; the headquarters and landing spot are not drawn on any map found.
new.t: Look on LiDAR and the 1938-39 aerials around the lake shore for the landing and the old grade. Much of the shore is homes now: ask first.
src: Frank A. King, Minnesota Logging Railroads (1981), pp 49-52 (leaf 51)
pinev: Lake identified from King ('now known as Lake Margaret'); pin at the lake, headquarters not placed (about 1 km).

new.n: Paine & Co. steam saw and planing mills, Carlton (1886-1900)
new.pl: Mill pond on Otter Creek beside the courthouse block (N 3rd-4th St), Carlton, Carlton County
new.st: King (1981): J. M. Paine ran a logging railroad and mill at Carlton from 1886 to 1900, reaching about 10 miles 'into the pine of Silver Brook Township'. The 1892 Sanborn map of Carlton shows 'Paine & Co's Steam Saw & Plan'g Mills' (gang and circular saws, 70,000 ft a day) on a mill pond on Otter Creek, with a 15-million-foot lumber yard; the pond borders the courthouse block.
new.t: Town land: look at the old mill pond edges and creek banks, and ask before detecting on any lot.
src: Frank A. King, Minnesota Logging Railroads (1981), pp 17-18
Sanborn Fire Insurance Map, Carlton, Minnesota, Sept 1892, sheets 2-3 (Library of Congress)
pinev: 1892 Sanborn puts the mill on a pond beside the courthouse block; pin estimated from the courthouse (about 400 m).
